newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines gets extension from IMF.
newsitem.headline: Philippines gets extension from IMF.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund has extended its three-year programme for the Philippines, Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson said on Thursday.
The extended fund facility was due to finish this month but Manila asked for an extension after it was unable to get necessary tax reforms through Congress in time.
"The IMF has agreed to a one-month technical extension to review the developments that transpired before agreeing to an extension up to year-end," Singson told reporters.
The government hopes its tax reforms, which have been opposed as too tough in the House of Representatives, will be passed by October.
The corporate and income tax bill is the last part of the comprehensive tax reform package to which Manila was committed under the IMF programme.
An IMF team is currently in the country to review the country's economic achievements.
"The developments have been favourable. Inflation is lower than expected. Base money is very much lower than the ceiling," Singson said.

Meanwhile, a Central Bank official said the IMF team was informed the government was downscaling its 1997 operating target for the budget surplus to 7.1 billion pesos, almost half of the 13 billion it earlier projected.

Budget officials had earlier said the lower surplus was due to the possibility of high tax exemptions based on the bill passed by the House of Representatives, lower privatisation proceeds and other factors.
